title: Apply for a Crypto Payment Gateway or Card Terminal
summary: Apply for the payment service your salon needs and follow its review and activation.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Apply for a VLINKPAY Crypto Payment Gateway or card terminal so your salon can prepare to accept these payment methods. Follow the application until the service is ready to use.

Before you start

Sign in with the salon owner’s account. Have the legal business details, authorized representative’s information, and required documents ready. You can save a draft while completing verification. Before submitting, the owner must finish identity and business verification with VLINKPAY (KYC/KYB).

1. Choose the service

Open Settings → Service Applications. Select Crypto payment gateway or Card terminal. These are separate applications.

2. Apply for a Crypto payment gateway

  1. Check the business information already filled in. Complete the crypto payment details, supported assets, and how you want to receive settlement funds using the options on the form.
  2. Upload the requested business documents and read the compliance information. If you choose settlement in USD, check which additional documents are required.
  3. If information is missing, save a draft and continue later. Before submitting, finish verification, complete the required items, upload documents, review authorization, and sign electronically with your full legal name.
  4. Select Apply for VLINKPAY Crypto Gateway and check the status. Follow the instructions from Nexora and VLINKPAY for review and setup.

3. Apply for a card terminal

  1. Check the business details and expected card-payment volume.
  2. Complete the terminal and delivery details, representative and ownership information, and how the salon will receive payments. Upload the documents requested for review.
  3. Read the agreements and authorization, complete verification, and add the required electronic signature.
  4. Select Submit terminal application and check the status. Nexora prepares and sends the authorized application to the card-processing partner.

Upload the required documents

Use PDF, PNG, JPG, or JPEG files. Each file can be up to 10 MB, with up to 5 files for each document type. Check the required documents for the options you selected.

4. Follow review and activation

  • Draft: Complete the missing information and submit when ready.
  • Nexora review / Provider review: Check the status and wait for the result.
  • Information needed: Read the reason, update the requested information, and resubmit.
  • Approved: The application is accepted; wait for service activation.
  • Active: The service has been activated. Follow the provider’s setup instructions before taking payments.
  • Rejected or Cancelled: Read the reason. If you need to apply again, select Start a new application when it is available.

Use the service after activation

An application is for registering the service. You take customer payments after the service is activated and set up. When a customer has paid on an external card terminal, record that payment separately in POS. The terminal application also leaves the salon’s Stripe Connect status unchanged.

Related: Set Up Ways to Receive Customer Payments · Take Payment and Give Customers a Receipt
keywords: Apply for a Crypto Payment Gateway or Card Terminal

title: Create and Update Appointments
summary: Book customers, check appointment times, and update services or technicians when needed.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

  • Help customers choose an appointment time with the service and staff member they want.
  • Help the front desk organize the salon schedule clearly throughout the day.

Before you start

Ask the customer to confirm their name, service, preferred time, and technician.

1. Open Appointments

Open Appointments and select the date you need.

2. Create an appointment

Select + New Booking, enter the customer and service details, then choose the date, time, and a suitable technician. You can leave the technician unassigned and choose one later.

3. Review or update an appointment

Find the customer's appointment. For a pending or confirmed appointment, select Reschedule to change the date, time, services, or technician. Check these details, then select Save Changes.

Check the result

  • The appointment appears on the correct date and time.
  • The customer, service, and staff member are correct.

If something does not work

  • If no time is available, check salon hours, service duration, and the staff schedule.
  • If the customer cannot be found, check the phone number first. Create a profile only if the customer does not already have one.

title: Check In Customers With or Without Appointments
summary: Record the customer’s arrival, check their services, and create a ticket for this visit.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Welcome customers promptly and help staff see who has arrived and which services they need.

Check-in records that a customer has arrived. A service ticket holds their details and the services they need for this visit.

Before you start

Use an account with front-desk access. Ask for the customer's name and phone number, and confirm whether they have an appointment. Check for an existing visit before creating another ticket.

For a customer with an appointment

  1. Open Tickets and select Not Arrived to see today's expected customers.
  2. Check the name, appointment time, and service. Select Check In on the correct appointment.
  3. Wait for the confirmation that the ticket is now waiting. Select Waiting and check the customer's ticket.

If the appointment is missing, open Appointments and verify the date and phone number before treating the customer as a walk-in.

For a walk-in customer

  1. Open Check-in, enter the customer's phone number, and select Continue.
  2. If today's appointments appear, choose the matching appointment. Use Check in without an appointment only when this is a separate visit without a booking.
  3. Enter or confirm the customer's name. Select services and a technician, or Anyone if the front desk will assign one. Services may be added later if the customer has not decided.
  4. Explain the text-message consent checkbox and ask whether the customer agrees to receive messages. The current form requires that checkbox; select it only after the customer agrees. Ask the owner for assistance if they decline.
  5. Select Check in if all details are entered on one page. If the screen takes you through several steps, continue to the final review before submitting.
  6. Check the confirmation and ticket number, select Done, then find the customer in Tickets.

Continue with an existing visit

If You already have ticket… appears for the same customer, choose That's me — I'm all set and use the existing ticket. Check in another guest is for a different person sharing the phone number.

Done: One ticket represents the visit and shows the correct customer and selected services. Check-in only confirms the customer's arrival. Next, assign staff, track service progress, and complete checkout.

Correct the phone number before check-in

If the phone number is wrong, correct it on the customer form. Press Enter or click outside the field. Nexora looks up the new valid number and clears the details entered for the previous number. Wait for the result, then check the customer's name, appointment, services, and technician before checking them in.

Choose service quantities and an eligible technician

  • Use + and − next to each selected service to adjust its quantity. Check the quantities and service total before check-in.
  • Choose a technician who can provide all selected services. If you change the services and the selected technician can no longer provide them all, Nexora clears that choice. Choose another technician or Anyone.
  • If the customer has not chosen services yet, you can check them in without selecting any. Confirm their services and prices with the front desk before checkout.

Next: Assign Waiting Customers with the Turn Board · Track Waiting Customers and Service Progress

title: Track Waiting Customers and Service Progress
summary: See who is waiting, which technician is working, and which services are finished before checkout.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Help front-desk staff and technicians see what stage each customer has reached and which services still need to be done.

Each ticket records the services for one customer visit. Check the services and technicians on the ticket, then follow progress in the Tickets list.

1. Find the customer’s ticket

Open Tickets. Use Not Arrived for today's appointments awaiting check-in, Waiting for checked-in customers, and In Service for visits being served. Open the customer's ticket and check their name, services, and technician.

2. Choose a technician for each service

On a service without a technician, select Choose Tech and choose a qualified staff member. To change the technician, use Change tech. When your selections are ready, select Assign Services to save the changes before continuing or leaving the ticket.

3. Check progress before checkout

Return to the Tickets list to see how many of the customer's services are done. If a service is waiting for a technician to accept it, the list also names the technician to check with.

Before checkout, ask the technicians which services are finished. For a ticket with several services, check each service and the person who provided it.

4. Continue to checkout

When the customer's services are finished, open the ticket, check that every service has the correct technician, and select Checkout. If the ticket is still Waiting, this changes it to In Service and opens the payment section. If you have just changed a technician, select Assign Services first.

Follow Take Payment and Give Customers a Receipt to verify payment and finish the order. After successful payment, find it in Completed Services.

If you cannot continue

  • Unsaved technician changes: Check the technician on each service, then select Assign Services. Unsaved selections may be lost when you leave the ticket.
  • A warning names services without a technician: Assign technicians to those services, save with Assign Services, and select Checkout.
  • The ticket is missing: Check the selected filter and whether the order has already been paid. Continue with the existing ticket for that visit.

Open Overview and Tickets

When you open Front Desk, Overview appears first. Review the salon’s activity here, then open Tickets to find a customer and update their services.

Review notes and photos after a service

If the technician added photos when completing a service, you can view them in the ticket, at checkout, or in completed-order details. Check the service name and read the notes before discussing the result with the customer. Photos added to general ticket notes appear separately.

Related: Check In Customers With or Without Appointments · Assign Waiting Customers with the Turn Board

title: Assign Waiting Customers with the Turn Board
summary: See which technicians are ready to work and assign services for waiting customers.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

The Turn Board helps front-desk staff assign waiting customers to technicians. Each technician can see which services they will provide.

Before you start

The customer must be checked in with a waiting ticket and an unassigned service. The technician must be set up to provide that service in the staff settings. Use an account with permission to manage front-desk operations.

1. Check that the technician is ready to work

Open Turn Board. Check the staff member's clock-in and busy status. If needed, review Staffs Clock before assigning work. Confirm both clock-in and availability before assigning a customer.

2. Choose a technician for a waiting customer

  1. In the view selector above the board, select Cards. If you are viewing Turn Grid, switch to Cards to see each technician's Assign Guest button.
  2. Find the intended staff member's card and select Assign Guest.
  3. In Assign next waiting guest, check the technician named at the top.
  4. Find the customer's row and verify the ticket number and service. Selecting the customer's row assigns the service to the technician immediately; there is no separate confirmation button.
  5. Wait for confirmation that the customer has been assigned and the selection window has closed. Open the customer's ticket in Tickets and verify the assigned technician on the service.

For example, choose an available manicure technician, select Assign Guest, then select the waiting customer's manicure ticket. Each selection assigns one service that this technician can provide and that has no technician yet. Review the remaining services separately on a multi-service ticket.

3. Check the assignment

Selecting a customer in Assign Guest saves that service assignment immediately. Open the ticket to check the technician and any services that still need one. If you choose or change another technician within the ticket, select Assign Services to save those changes.

Follow Track Waiting Customers and Service Progress to review progress and continue to checkout when the customer is finished.

If no guest appears

  • Check that the ticket is Waiting and has a service without an assigned technician.
  • Open Staff, select the staff member, and check Services to confirm that the service is selected.
  • If the service is already assigned, open its ticket and use Change tech, then save with Assign Services. Continue using the customer's existing ticket.

Done: The intended technician appears on the correct service, and the team knows which services still need assignment.

Related: Check In Customers With or Without Appointments

title: Take Payment and Give Customers a Receipt
summary: Check the services, total, and money received, then print or send the customer’s receipt.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Help cashiers check the amount due, confirm payment, and provide a receipt the customer can keep.

Before you start

Use an account with checkout access. Confirm the customer's services are finished and each service has the correct staff member. An appointment reserves a time. The service ticket records the visit. After payment is completed, the order moves to the completed list.

Give a price estimate before service (optional)

If the customer wants a price first, open Estimate. Select + Add on services in the catalog, then check quantities and the estimated total. For a one-time service, select + Custom, enter its name and price, and select Add to estimate.

Tax and tips are not included in the estimate; confirm final prices and discounts at checkout. When the customer agrees and has no ticket for this visit yet, select Check in with this service or Check in with these services. Enter the customer's name and phone number, then select Confirm check-in. Check the ticket number after success.

1. Review the order

Open Tickets and choose the correct customer. If the order is already In Service, you can also open it from Checkout Customer.

Check the customer, services, staff, discounts, tax, tip, and total. Select View beside the customer's name if you need their contact details or previous visits.

  • To add a service from the catalog, select + Add services, then + Add on the service. If the catalog is already open beside the ticket, choose the service there.
  • For a service that is not in the catalog, select + Custom. In the window that opens, enter its name and a price above $0, choose a technician if known, then select Add to ticket. Check the name, price, and technician on the ticket. The service applies only to this ticket.
  • Check that every service has the correct technician. If you have just chosen or changed a technician, select Assign Services to save, then select Checkout to open the payment section.

Correct any wrong details or amounts before collecting payment.

2. Choose a payment method

Choose the customer's Payment Method. Direct payment apps appear only when the salon has enabled and configured them. Select More to see these options.

  • Cash: Count the money and enter Cash received. Check how much change to give the customer. The amount entered must cover the total.
  • Card: Check that payment succeeded on the terminal before recording it as received.
  • Zelle, Cash App, Venmo, Apple Cash, PayPal, or VLINKPAY Wallet: Show the receiving details or QR code if available, then check that the money arrived in the salon's account. VLINKPAY Wallet here also relies on the cashier confirming receipt.
  • Gift Card or Crypto: Continue with the receipt and confirmation steps below to open VlinkPay, then follow its payment instructions.
  • Split Pay: Check that the saved portions cover the total and that every portion was received.

3. Choose how to provide the receipt and finish

  1. Choose Send SMS, Print, or No Receipt before selecting Pay or Mark as received. SMS requires a customer phone number; confirm that number with the customer. Printing requires a configured printer.
  2. For Cash, Card, or Split Pay, select Pay with the displayed amount only after receiving all the money. For a direct payment app, select Mark as received after checking that the money arrived. For Gift Card or Crypto, select Pay to continue to VlinkPay.
  3. In Confirm payment, check the amount and method, then select Confirm payment. If either is wrong, select Cancel to go back.
  4. For Gift Card or Crypto, wait for VlinkPay to open, follow its instructions, and wait for successful payment confirmation.
  5. Wait for the completion screen showing the paid amount and payment status. Confirm the order appears in Completed Services.

Choosing a receipt option only saves your selection. Check that payment has completed before finishing the transaction. If a warning names services without a technician or unsaved changes, choose the technicians, save with Assign Services, and continue.

If there is a problem with the receipt or payment

  • No paper receipt: Use Print Receipt or Re-print on the completed order. Check Receipt Printing if needed. Reprinting uses the existing paid order and requires no additional payment.
  • No SMS receipt: Check the phone number and use the existing order details when asking support to review delivery.
  • No payment confirmation: Check the completed order list and the payment provider's record before retrying. If money was received but the order is not marked as paid, ask the owner or support to compare the order with the payment received.
  • Incorrect completed payment: Give the owner or support the order number, method, amount, and provider reference. Use only a refund procedure confirmed by the payment provider or support; editing or deleting a ticket alone does not return funds.

Check Gift Card and Crypto Card details on the receipt

If a confirmed payment includes Gift Card or Crypto Card details, check the success screen or printed receipt for the last 4 digits of the card number, amount paid, and remaining balance. The rest of the card number is hidden. Check the balance currency as well, since a Crypto Card balance may be shown in a currency other than USD.

Printing the receipt shows the payment already completed and does not charge the card again. If the balance is missing, ask support to check the existing payment record. You do not need to take another payment to check the balance.

Related: Set Up Ways to Receive Customer Payments · Review Collected Payments and Salon Reports

title: Find Customer Details and Previous Visits
summary: Find the customer’s profile, review earlier services, and update contact details confirmed with the customer.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Help front-desk staff and technicians see which services a customer had and who provided them, so they can prepare for this visit.

1. Find the correct profile

  1. Open Customer History.
  2. Enter the customer's name or phone number in Search. Confirm the phone number with the customer if names are similar.
  3. Select View on the matching row. Check the contact details, total visits, and last visit.
  4. Review Ticket & Appointment History for previous services, dates, and staff. Go to the next history page to see more visits.

2. Update confirmed information

The owner can select Edit in the profile when the salon’s customer management is connected. Change only the details the customer confirms, such as their name, phone number, or email. Check the phone's country code, select Save changes, and reopen the profile to verify the saved result.

Staff should ask the owner to update the profile. If the owner cannot see Edit, contact support to check the salon’s customer-management connection. Continue using the existing profile to keep the customer's visits together.

Example: help a returning customer

A customer says they visited last month and would like the same service. Search their phone number, select View, and check the previous service and technician. Confirm what they want before booking or choosing a technician for this visit. If their email has changed, the owner can use Edit → Save changes when Edit is available, then check the updated email.

If you cannot find the details you need

  • No match: Check the spelling and phone number, clear the search, and try again.
  • Similar or duplicate profiles: Compare contact details and visit history. Ask the owner or support to identify the correct profile and explain whether and how the profiles can be combined or removed before you make changes.
  • A visit is missing: Check the profile and history pages first. If the visit still needs review, share the customer and visit details with support without changing the existing appointment or order.

Done: The correct profile is open and staff can locate the visit needed to help the customer. If details needed updating, the owner has saved and checked the changes.

Import an existing customer list

In Customer History, select Import Excel / CSV / JSON to upload your list. Choose the phone-number column, check the preview, and review which customers were added or skipped. See Import Customers from CSV, Excel, or JSON.

Related: Create and Update Appointments · Check In Customers With or Without Appointments

title: Review Collected Payments and Salon Reports
summary: See how much the salon collected, how customers paid, and whether the figures match paid orders.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

See how much the salon collected, how customers paid, and whether completed orders match the day's payment records.

1. Choose the reporting period

Open Store Income Report using an account with report access. Choose Day, Week, Year, or a date range. Start with one day when checking a specific sale.

Paid, completed orders appear under the date and time they were completed, using the salon's time zone. The appointment date does not determine the sales date, and unpaid tickets are not included in this report.

2. Check each amount in the report

  • Total collected: The recorded order total after discounts, including products, tax, and tips. Refunds have not been subtracted from this figure. Use this figure to check order totals. To confirm bank deposits, check bank statements. To calculate profit, also check salon expenses.
  • Sales tax and Tips: Already included in the collected total.
  • Payment breakdown: Amounts recorded under each method, such as Card, Cash, Gift Card, Crypto, Zelle, Cash App, Venmo, VLINKPAY Wallet, Apple Cash, and PayPal. If a customer pays partly in cash and partly by card, the same order may count as a transaction under both methods.
  • Supply Fee and Merchant Fee: Review these alongside other business expenses when calculating profit. Confirm the Merchant Fee using the payment provider's statement.
  • Return Transactions: In Day view, this shows the number and amount of successful card refunds recorded in Nexora. Refunds appear on the salon’s local refund date, rather than the original sale date. Use the payment provider’s records to reconcile these amounts and any cash refunds or refunds made outside Nexora.

3. Compare with service sales

Open Service Income Report to see sales for each service. Net service sales are service charges after discounts on individual services and on the whole order. Products, tax, and tips are reported separately. To calculate profit, also account for the salon's expenses.

Example: $100 in services − $10 discount + $20 in products + $5.50 tax + $15 tip = $130.50 collected. Net service sales are $90. The collected total includes products, tax, and tips; net service sales include only services after discounts.

4. Compare payments and save the report

  1. Open Completed Services and compare one order's total and payment method with the same day's report.
  2. Compare the reported cash amount with the cash in the drawer. Compare electronic payments with records from the payment provider. Check fees, refund activity, and deposit timing separately.
  3. Select Print / PDF to download the report. To email it, select Email, check the recipient, and select Send report.

If figures differ

Check the selected dates, salon time zone, order completion status, discounts, and payment method first. For help reconciling a difference, share the period and order number with the owner or support and leave the original payment details unchanged.

Related: Take Payment and Give Customers a Receipt · Review Each Technician’s Work and Earnings

title: Review Each Technician’s Work and Earnings
summary: Check services, commission, tips, and deductions before calculating how much to pay each technician.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Help the owner and staff review completed services, commission, tips, and deductions before agreeing on the amount to pay.

1. Open the technician report

Open Technician Report and choose a day, week, or month. Here, Technician means the staff member providing services. Use an account with permission to view the relevant staff records.

2. Read the main columns

  • Turns and Hours: Activity and time recorded for the selected period. Use the hours to review recorded work time. To confirm wages already paid, check bank transfers or signed cash receipts.
  • Service $: Service sales attributed to that staff member.
  • Comm % and Commission: The commission percentage and calculated amount. Supply fees are deducted from the service amount used to calculate commission. Comm % shows the rate currently set; earlier periods may have been paid at a different rate.
  • Tip: Tips allocated to the staff member.
  • Tech discount: Only the portion of discounts assigned to the staff member.
  • Supply Fee: Total supply fees deducted from service sales before commission is calculated.
  • Day / Days: Days in the period when the technician took a ticket, completed a service, or had an assigned appointment, using the salon’s time zone. Appointments count on their scheduled date. Clocking in alone does not count as a day in this column.
  • Clean Fee: Deducted once for each qualifying day in the Day / Days column, including a day with an assigned appointment. Each day uses the rate effective on that date; days before the fee was first set are $0. If the rate changed during the period, the total may differ from Days multiplied by the current rate. It is already subtracted from Tech Receives.
  • Tech Receives: Commission plus the tips assigned to the technician, minus their share of discounts and the clean fee. If the result is below zero, the report shows zero. Check the salon's payment records, such as bank transfers or signed cash receipts, to confirm the amount already paid.
  • Weekly guarantee: For Weekly salary, this column shows the saved weekly salary amount; for Agreed amount, it shows the agreed amount. It is shown separately and is not added to Tech Receives. Check the salon's pay agreement when calculating the final amount due.
  • Pay structure: The tag under each technician's name shows their configured pay structure, such as Commission, Weekly salary, or Agreed amount.

Example: a flat commission arrangement

For $100 in service sales and a $10 supply fee, the commission base is $90. At 60%, commission is $54. Add $15 in allocated tips and subtract $5 in staff-borne discounts and a $2 clean fee for 1 day worked: Tech Receives = $62.

The supply fee is already accounted for in the $90 commission base. This example covers a flat commission arrangement. For a complete payroll review, combine this report with the salon's agreed salary, hourly pay, and guarantee calculations.

3. Check details before paying staff

  1. In Daily or Weekly mode, select View beside the staff member to see the services and amounts included in the report.
  2. Compare the service assignment, tip allocation, and discount share with completed orders.
  3. Review the agreed settings in Staff → Role, Pay & Tips. If pay settings have changed, amounts for an earlier period may be recalculated using the current settings. Check changes to pay, commission, and tips when comparing with a saved report.
  4. Use Export CSV to keep the table. Use Print all in Daily, Weekly, or Monthly mode to print reports for several technicians. Owners can use Send mail all in Daily or Weekly mode. In an individual staff member’s Daily or Weekly detail, accounts with report access can use Print or Send mail.

Compare calculated earnings with money already paid

Use the report to check calculated staff earnings. Compare bank transfers or signed cash receipts to confirm how much the salon has already paid. Check the dates, who provided each service, supply fees, clean fees and days worked, commission rates, tips, and each staff member's share of discounts. If figures differ, review them with the owner to agree on the amount due before payment.

Related: Set Up Tax, Tips, and Supply Fees · Review Collected Payments and Salon Reports

title: Issue Gift Cards and Membership Cards in POS
summary: Open the VlinkPay card page from the owner account and reconnect if needed.
htmlContent:
Benefits for the owner

Gift Card Center lets the owner open VlinkPay’s card-issuing page directly in Front Desk.

Before you start

Sign in as the salon Owner and select the correct business. Only the owner can open Gift Card Center.

1. Open Gift Card Center

  1. Open Front Desk → Gift Card Center.
  2. Wait while the page shows Connecting to VLINKPAY….
  3. Check that VLINKPAY connected appears and the Issue Digital page has loaded.
  4. Follow the instructions on the VlinkPay page to work with cards. Check the result before repeating an action.

2. Reconnect if the page does not load

If you see a connection error or a message that the VLINKPAY session has expired, select Retry. Wait for the connected status and card page to return. If the problem continues, check the owner account and selected business, then contact support with the error message.

Check the result

You should see both the connected status and the card page. Opening the page is the first step; complete the card or payment steps in VlinkPay and check the transaction result there.

Related: Take Payment and Give Customers a Receipt
keywords: Issue Gift Cards and Membership Cards in POS

title: Import Customers from CSV, Excel, or JSON
summary: Upload a customer list, choose the matching columns, and check the import result.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Bring your existing customer list into Nexora so staff can find customer details in one place. Check the import result to see which customers were added.

Before you start

Use an account with permission to manage salon customers. Prepare a .csv, .xlsx, or .json file up to 10 MB with customer phone numbers. Check the phone numbers, dates, and contact details before uploading.

1. Upload the file

  1. Open Customer History and select Import Excel / CSV / JSON.
  2. Choose the file and wait for Nexora to check it. Customers are added only after you confirm the import.
  3. Select Continue to choose the customer columns.

2. Choose customer columns and review the preview

  1. For Excel, select the sheet containing your customers. For Excel or CSV, check which row contains the column names. JSON uses one list and does not ask you to select a header row.
  2. Choose the phone-number column for Phone Number. This is required. Choose matching columns for Customer Name, Email, Date of Birth, Created, and Last Visit if you want to include them.
  3. Use each file column for only one type of customer information. Select Skip for anything you do not want to import. Check your choices again if you change the sheet or header row.
  4. The preview shows a few sample rows. Check the details and warnings before importing. The result for the whole file appears after the import finishes.

3. Import and review the result

  1. When the columns match, select Import customers once and wait for the result.
  2. Check Total rows, Imported, Duplicates, and Invalid. A customer may be skipped if they appear more than once in the file, already exist in the salon’s list, or have an invalid phone number.
  3. If customers were skipped, select Download CSV report to read the reasons. Correct the file where needed and check it before importing again.
  4. Select Done, then open Customer History and search for a newly imported customer to verify the result.

If the import stops or adds no customers

If you lose the connection or see a timeout message, refresh the page and check the customer list before trying again. Some customers may already have been added. If all rows are duplicates or invalid, no new customers will be added. Check the counts and the reasons in the report.

Before sending marketing messages

Check that customers have agreed to receive marketing messages before using the imported list for messaging. Adding someone to the list does not mean they have given consent.

Related: Find Customer Details and Previous Visits
keywords: Import Customers from CSV, Excel, or JSON

title: Let Customers Check In with a QR Code
summary: Set up a separate check-in QR code or One QR so customers can record their arrival on their own phones.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

  • Customers use their own phones to check in and let the salon know they have arrived.
  • Allow front-desk staff to spend more time welcoming and serving customers.

Choose how customers check in

Your salon can offer either of these options for customers using their phones:

  • A separate check-in QR code: Customers scan it to open the salon’s check-in page directly.
  • One QR: Customers scan the salon’s One QR code, then select Smart Check-in.

Both options let customers check in on their own phones. If the salon uses a shared tablet, follow Set Up a Customer Check-In Tablet to connect it. The pairing QR code connects the tablet to the salon. Customers using their phones scan the salon’s check-in QR code or One QR code.

Before you start

Have a phone with a camera and an internet connection ready. Choose a spot where customers can easily see the QR code.

If the customer already has a ticket for this visit, use that ticket to avoid a duplicate check-in. When testing both options, check for an existing ticket before submitting another request.

Option 1: Use a separate check-in QR code

  1. Open QR Self Check-in.
  2. Check the salon details, then download or print the QR code shown.
  3. Scan the code with your own phone. Check the salon name, enter your name and contact details, then submit the check-in.
  4. At the front desk, check that the name you used appears in the customer list.

Option 2: Let customers check in through One QR

  1. Open One QR and select Customer.
  2. Make sure Smart Check-in is enabled. If it is missing, select Add module to add it, then enable it.
  3. Select Save settings, then scan the salon’s One QR code with your own phone.
  4. On the One QR page, select Smart Check-in or the custom name your salon uses for this option. Check that it opens the correct salon’s check-in page, enter your details, and submit.
  5. At the front desk, check that the name you used appears in the customer list.

Customers follow these steps on their own phones. See Set Up One QR for Customers to prepare and print the One QR code.

Display the QR code

Place your chosen QR code where arriving customers can easily see and scan it. For One QR, tell customers: “Scan this code with your phone, then choose Smart Check-in.”

Check the result

  • If using a separate check-in QR code, it opens the correct salon’s check-in page.
  • If using One QR, customers can see Smart Check-in and open the correct salon’s check-in page.
  • Front-desk staff can find the name used for the test check-in in the customer list.
  • If the salon offers both options, each one has been scanned and checked.

If something does not work

  • If the code does not open, check the phone’s internet connection and whether the printed code is clear.
  • If the check-in option is missing from One QR, check that you selected Customer, added Smart Check-in, enabled it, and saved the settings.
  • If the name does not appear at the front desk, check that the check-in was submitted successfully, then refresh the customer list.

Create a check-in poster

  1. Open Public Check-in QR and choose a ready-made poster or a customizable template.
  2. Ready-made posters use portrait Letter size. For a customizable template, choose an available size, language, and design, then check the salon details in the preview.
  3. Wait for the preview and images to load, then print the poster or download it as a PDF or PNG. You can also download just the QR code image.
  4. Scan the final printed or exported QR code to confirm that it opens the correct salon’s check-in page.

Check the customer check-in page

Make sure the salon’s public page and Public Check-in are enabled. On a phone or public kiosk, customers can check in for an appointment only when check-in is available. If it is too early, follow the message or ask the front desk to check the appointment before creating another visit. You can use a public kiosk link or pair a tablet with a PIN; see Set Up a Customer Check-In Tablet.

title: Create and Apply Promotions
summary: Enter a discount, choose the days and times it applies, and check the offer on the order before taking payment.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Attract more customers during quieter days and times with an offer they can easily understand.

1. Create the offer

  1. Open Promotions with an account that can manage offers. Select Add promotion, or Use this template to start from a sample.
  2. Enter Promotion name and a clear description. Select Percent · % or Amount · $, then enter the discount value.
  3. Select the days and start/end times in the salon's local time. The end must be later than the start on the same day.
  4. Review the banners and where the offer will appear. A new promotion, including one created from a template, is disabled by default. To review it before enabling it, leave Offer this at checkout unchecked and select Save promotion. If you check this box before saving, the promotion is enabled as soon as it is saved.

2. Check the offer and turn it on

Find the saved offer, select Preview, and check the wording and schedule. Use Edit to correct it. When staff know the discount and when it applies, select Enable promotion. Use Disable when it should no longer be offered.

Example: a weekday service discount

Create “Tuesday service savings”: 10% off service charges, Tuesday, 10 AM–2 PM. For $100 in services with no other discounts, the discount is $10 and services become $90 before tax and tip. Product charges are separate.

Important: The checkout promotion applies to the total service charges. Describe the offer as a discount on the total service charges, and check the amount before collecting payment. The description explains the offer to customers. Writing conditions there does not create discount rules for individual services.

3. Apply the offer when the customer qualifies

Open the customer's order in Checkout Customer, select Discount all, and find Offers this visit qualifies for. Select the offer to apply it, then check the discount and total before payment.

The system checks the offer against the date and time the customer checked in, using the salon’s local time. For the example, confirm that the customer checked in on Tuesday within the offer's time window. Apply one promotion to the order at a time. Selecting a different promotion replaces the one already selected.

If the offer is missing or incorrect

Check its enabled status, days, time window, and the visit's check-in time. Review the offer and any other discounts on the order before collecting payment. To try checkout before serving customers, contact support for guidance.

Related: Review Each Step from Arrival to Checkout · Set Up Tax, Tips, and Supply Fees

title: Review Ratings and Follow Up on Customer Feedback
summary: Read ratings and comments to see what customers liked, what needs attention, and who will follow up.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

  • Help the owner and technicians see which services and parts of the visit customers liked.
  • Help the team identify what to improve and choose someone to follow up.

Before you start

Choose a regular time for the owner or manager to review feedback.

1. Open Reviews

Open Reviews.

2. Filter the list

Use the available source, rating, or staff filters to focus on the feedback you need.

3. Review comments

Read the rating and comment. Note what customers liked and what the team can improve.

4. Agree on who will follow up and what to do

Discuss the feedback with the manager or staff member responsible and agree on what to do next. Share only the customer details needed to address it.

Check the result

  • Recent feedback has been reviewed.
  • Someone has been assigned to follow up on each concern that needs further attention.

If something does not work

  • If no feedback appears, check the selected filters.
  • Handle sensitive customer information according to salon policy.

title: Set Up One QR for Customers
summary: Bring the salon’s customer options into one QR code so customers can scan it and choose what they need.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

One QR brings the salon’s customer options and links together. Customers scan one code at reception or on printed materials to choose what they need.

Before you start

Use an account with access to One QR. Decide which options customers should see and have any custom links ready.

1. Open One QR and select Customer

Open One QR and select Customer. Check the selected group before making changes.

2. Add, arrange, and customize tiles

  1. Add the services you want to offer, enable the ready ones, and arrange them in the order customers should see.
  2. Edit Tile label to use a clear name. For a custom link, enter a complete HTTPS address in Link address.
  3. Select Change icon to choose an icon, or Upload to add a PNG, JPG, or WebP image. Nexora reduces the file size automatically. Check how it looks in the preview.
  4. Select Save settings. If a tile has an input error, correct the highlighted label or address and save again.

3. Remove a tile

Select Remove and read the confirmation before continuing. Removing a tile saves the entire list for the selected group, including other valid changes you have made. Tiles with missing information or errors are left out. Finish and save any tiles you want to keep before removing another one.

4. Preview, download, and scan

  1. Check that your One QR is Active. If it is Paused, turn it back on using the switch on the QR card.
  2. Preview the customer page and check the salon name, labels, icons, and enabled tiles.
  3. Select View QR & Download, then Download QR PNG. Scan the downloaded QR image with your phone.
  4. Open each visible tile and confirm it reaches the intended page before printing or displaying the code.

If something does not work

  • If a tile is missing, check the selected audience, its enabled setting, whether the last save succeeded, and whether One QR is active.
  • If a link is rejected, use a complete HTTPS address and correct the indicated error.
  • If a service is not ready, disable its tile and save. If the printed code is hard to scan, use a larger, sharp code with strong contrast.

Related: Let Customers Check In with a QR Code

title: Review Tips by Technician and QR Code
summary: See tips for each technician and QR code to recognize contributions and review code placement.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Review tips for each staff member and QR code to recognize staff contributions and decide whether a code needs a more visible location.

1. Open the tip figures

Open Analytics. This page shows tip amounts, technician rankings by tips, and tips received through each QR code. Sales and staff earnings are covered in their respective reports. For completed salon sales, use Review Collected Payments and Salon Reports.

Daily Revenue Trend automatically shows daily tips for the latest seven days; this page has no date-range selector. Before comparing other totals or rankings with this chart, check whether they cover the same dates. If the dates are not shown, ask support which period those figures cover.

2. Check tips by day, technician, and QR code

  • Daily Revenue Trend: On a computer, move the pointer over the chart to see the tip amount for each day.
  • How Tips Were Paid: See which payment methods customers used for tips.
  • Leaderboard: Review staff tip amounts and counts. Use these figures to recognize contributions, alongside customer feedback and hours worked for a fuller view.
  • Station Performance: Compare the displayed top stations by tip amount. A station is a QR code saved under a name, such as “Reception.” Tip amounts do not tell you how many customers visited the salon or scanned the code.

Example: make the reception QR easier to find

If the reception station appears in Station Performance, record its displayed tip total and the date. Check that its QR code is readable and placed where customers can easily see it. Ask the owner to approve any placement change; review your stations under One QR → Receive Tips.

Record the same station's total again after seven days. For example, if a cumulative total rises from $40 to $60, the increase for that week is $20. Compare one seven-day period with another. Also note changes in customer visits or staffing, since these can affect tips.

If figures are missing

Check that you are viewing the correct salon and that tipping activity has been recorded. The list shows the top stations by tip amount. If a station is missing, open its settings to check whether it is active. Refresh the page after more tips are received and share the relevant details with support if records need further review.

Next step: Choose one change to try, such as moving the QR code to a more visible spot. Record today's tip total and check it again after seven days.

Related: Set Up One QR for Customers · Review Each Technician’s Work and Earnings

title: Set Up AI Voice and Send Customer Text Messages
summary: Set up AI call answering and prepare customer text messages after the salon’s services are activated.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

AI Voice helps answer customer calls. Text messages let the salon share services and offers with customers who have agreed to receive them.

Before you start

The owner should approve the service plan and messaging budget. Prepare accurate salon information, a phone you can use for a test call, and customer groups that have agreed to receive your messages.

Part 1: Set up AI Voice to answer calls

  1. Open AI Hub → Plans. Check for Current Active Plan. If you only see Trial request submitted, your request has been sent, but service activation has not yet been confirmed. Wait for service activation and an assigned AI phone number before setting up forwarding.
  2. If the plan or voice service is not available, choose a service plan and follow the instructions on that page to sign up. Then ask support to confirm that AI Voice is active and provide your salon's AI phone number. Set up call forwarding only after the assigned number is confirmed.
  3. Open AI Voice setup guide. This guide explains how to forward calls from the salon's phone number to its AI number. Select the instructions for your carrier and choose whether AI answers immediately or after the salon phone rings. Replace [AI NUMBER] in the instructions with your assigned AI phone number.
  4. Call the salon number from another phone. Check that AI answers at the time you selected and gives the correct greeting and salon information.
  5. Open Call Log and find the call. If you requested an appointment, verify its details in Appointments and compare the customer name, service, date, and time with what you requested during the call.

If calls do not reach AI, review the carrier and forwarding choice. If the AI answers with incorrect information, ask support to correct the setup before promoting the number.

Register the SMS sender before using it

Open Settings → Service Applications and select SMS registration. Make sure the AI Voice plan and assigned phone number are active. See Register SMS Service and Track Your Application to complete and submit the application. Wait for approval before using the registered sender. SMS Credits pay for messages; Ads Credit pays for advertising. See Add Ads Credit and Review Activity.

Part 2: Write and send text messages to a customer group

  1. Open SMS Campaigns. If this tab is unavailable, return to Plans and ask support to check service activation. Check SMS Credits, the balance available to send messages.
  2. Select Create New Campaign. Name this message campaign, choose the customers who will receive it, and write a short message. Check any offer link and the phone-shaped preview on the screen.
  3. Choose Send now or a future schedule. Check how many customers will receive the message, its length, the estimated SMS Credits needed, and the send time. Use only recipients who agreed to receive these messages and keep the instructions that tell customers how to stop receiving messages.
  4. After the owner approves the message, recipients, and send time, select Send Campaign. With Send now, this starts sending immediately, so finish your review before selecting it. The preview shows the message on screen; it does not send a message.
  5. Check campaign history and use View for recipient results. Scheduled means the campaign is waiting for its selected send time. Use recipient results to confirm delivery. Check which messages failed and why before deciding whether to send them again.

When getting started, you can write and preview the message without selecting Send Campaign. After sending, confirm delivery using recipient results and an intended recipient's phone.

Related: Set Up Online Booking · Find Customer Details and Previous Visits

title: Add Ads Credit and Review Activity
summary: Check your advertising balance, add credit, and review top-ups and spending.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Ads Credit lets the salon set aside money for advertising. Check how much is available, add credit when needed, and review top-ups and spending.

Before you start

Use an account with access to Package Management and Ads Credit. The owner should confirm the advertising budget and payment method. Use SMS Credits separately for text messages.

1. Check your balance and recent activity

Open Package Management → Ads Credit. If Package Management is missing from your menu, use this link to open Ads Credit directly. Check Available Ads Credit for credit you can use, Credit on hold for credit being held, and Recorded spend for spending already recorded. Review the activity list for recent transactions.

2. Add Ads Credit

  1. Select Add Ads Credit and enter an amount within the minimum and maximum shown.
  2. Choose an available wallet or card payment method. Check the amount and currency.
  3. Read and accept the terms, then confirm payment. The amount is charged to the payment method you selected.
  4. Wait for the payment result. If you pay by card, complete the provider’s payment steps and wait while Nexora checks the transaction.

3. Check the result

  • After a successful payment, check the new balance and top-up in the activity list.
  • If payment fails, read the message and check the payment record before trying again.
  • If the payment is still pending or you lose the connection, check activity and your wallet or card transaction before paying again. Contact support with the transaction details if the result is unclear.

Use your advertising credit

  • Ads Credit is prepaid credit for advertising. Read the terms for usage and refunds. You cannot transfer or withdraw this balance.
  • Each top-up is a payment you choose to make. It does not set up automatic recurring payments.
  • After adding credit, continue the setup and approval steps for any draft campaign you want to run. A paused campaign can resume only if its existing approval, schedule, and budget allow it.
  • Use SMS Credits to pay for text messages and check SMS registration approval separately. Ads Credit covers advertising.

Related: Set Up AI Voice and Send Customer Text Messages · Register SMS Service and Track Your Application

title: Post a Nail Technician Job and Manage It in POS
summary: Create a job posting, submit it to NailHub for free, share the link, and manage recruitment from POS.
htmlContent:
Benefits for your salon

Create a nail technician job posting from POS, submit it to NailHub for free, and manage your postings from the same place you manage your salon.

Watch the video: post a nail technician job (2 minutes, in Vietnamese).

Before you start

Use your salon owner account. Check the salon name, address, and phone number in Salon Information. Add a phone number before saving a draft or submitting a posting. Your salon name and phone number will be public on the published posting.

1. Open recruitment

From the left menu, select POS, open Salon Settings and Staff, then switch to Recruitment. Select Post a Job. The form has three steps: Compose, Preview, and Result.

2. Describe the role

  1. Turn on Mark as urgent if you need someone soon. The posting will show an Urgent badge.
  2. Enter a clear Job title, such as “Nail technician with multiple skills wanted”. Choose the Position and enter the Number of openings.
  3. Choose the Work schedule: Full-time, Part-time, or Flexible. Apply by is optional; leave it empty if you have no deadline.
  4. Select Choose from salon menu, choose the services the new hire will provide, then select Apply selection. Review the suggested Desired skills; remove or add skills that fit the role, such as Acrylic, Gel, Pedicure, or Dip.

3. Add pay, posting content, and photos

  1. Under Salary type, choose Guaranteed, No guaranteed, or Negotiable. If you choose Guaranteed, enter the Weekly Salary ($).
  2. Write the Posting content to explain the work, schedule, requirements, benefits, and how to apply. Give technicians enough detail to decide whether to contact you.
  3. Add a Cover image and salon Images if needed. Wait for the photos to finish uploading. The Quick preview updates as you fill in the form.

If you are not ready to submit, complete the required fields and select Save draft. Later, open Draft and select Continue editing.

4. Review and submit

  1. Select Preview posting. Review the title, content, skills, schedule, number of openings, pay, and photos.
  2. Check Public contact details, including your salon name and phone number. Anyone visiting NailHub can see these details. Select Back to edit if you need to make changes.
  3. When everything is correct, check I have reviewed the content and the contact information., then select Post to NailHub.
  4. When you see Submitted for review, select Back to My Posts to track it. The posting appears under Recruiting once it is approved.

5. Open the posting and share its link

Return to Recruitment in POS, or open Community and My Posts. Filter by Recruiting, then select View posting in POS or View on NailHub in Community to check the approved posting.

Copy the NailHub posting link to share it on Facebook, in communities, or on your salon website.

6. Edit or close recruitment

  • Use All, Recruiting, Draft, Pending review, and Closed to find your posting. You can also search by keyword.
  • Select Edit on a posting that can still be edited, review the changes, and submit them. A previously submitted posting returns to Pending review and stays unavailable on NailHub until it is approved again.
  • When you have filled the openings, select Close recruitment, read the message, and confirm. The posting stops accepting new applications and disappears from the job board. A closed posting cannot be edited or reopened.

If something does not work

  • You cannot save a draft or open the preview: Correct the fields showing errors, check the salon phone number, and wait for photo uploads to finish. The title needs 10–60 characters; the content needs 100–5,000 characters; openings must be a whole number from 1–99. The deadline cannot be in the past. For Guaranteed pay, enter a weekly amount greater than 0 with at most two decimal places.
  • No salon services appear: Check for active services in Services, then return to the menu selection.
  • A photo will not upload: Use JPEG, PNG, or WebP images, up to 5 MB each. You can add one cover image and up to 6 images inside the posting. Try again or remove the photo that did not upload.
  • Submitting fails: Read the message and try again; your form content is kept. If the status has changed, return to the list and reopen the posting.
  • The posting is missing on NailHub: Check Pending review. If you cannot find it in your list, choose All and clear the search keywords.

After hiring a technician

See Add Staff and Set Their Services and Hours to set up the staff member in your salon.

title: Connect Your Technician Account to a Salon
summary: Accept a salon invitation, check your connection, and select the services you can perform.
htmlContent:
Benefits for technicians

Connect your account to the right salon to see your assigned appointments and service tickets. If you work at several salons, you can check each one from your technician account.

Before you start

Sign in with your own account and open the technician workspace. Check that your profile includes your name and contact details so the salon owner can identify you.

1. Accept an invitation or request to join

  1. Open My Salons. If the salon has invited you, find Link Requests.
  2. Check the salon name and invited role. Select Accept for the salon where you work, or Decline if the invitation is incorrect.
  3. If there is no invitation, ask the owner to invite you or scan the salon’s staff invitation QR and follow the instructions. If your request is awaiting approval, ask the owner to check it.
  4. Return to My Salons and check that your salon connection is active before opening your assigned work.

2. Check your display name and services

  1. At the correct salon, select Edit Work Skill, choose the services you can perform, and select Save. Agree on this list with the owner so the front desk can assign suitable work.
  2. To change your name at this salon, select Edit Nickname. This name applies only at that salon; leave it blank to use your original name.
  3. Check your Level if the owner has assigned one. When you are clocked in at the salon, its card shows Clocked in.
  4. Select Work Order to see assigned tickets, or open My Calendar to see appointments.

What should the salon and technician agree on?

The owner checks the staff member and salon connection. You check your display name and the services you can perform. Agree on working hours, and ask the person managing the salon schedule to update them when needed.

When you need to unlink from a salon

For an active salon connection, select Unlink, check the salon name, and read the message before confirming. You will lose the tip QR for this salon. If the salon still owes you tip payouts, you cannot unlink yet. Ask the owner to settle the balance, then try again.

Let the owner know first, and use Unlink only when you no longer work at the salon.

If the salon or your work is unavailable

Check that you are using the correct account, have accepted the invitation, and have an active connection. If approval is still pending or the salon name is wrong, give the owner your account name and the salon name to check.

Related: Add Staff and Set Their Services and Hours · View and Accept Your Assigned Tickets · Coordinate with Your Salon During a Shift

title: View and Accept Your Assigned Tickets
summary: Find the right ticket in My Tickets, review the customer’s requests, and accept or decline an assigned service.
htmlContent:
Benefits for technicians

See which customers and services are assigned to you, then confirm that you can take the work so the front desk can continue arranging customers.

What are Tickets and Work Orders?

A ticket records a customer’s details and services for a salon visit. In your technician account, My Tickets lists tickets assigned to you. Opening a ticket shows the Work Order screen, where you can review and manage your services. Several technicians may perform different services on the same ticket.

1. Find the right ticket

  1. Sign in to your technician account and open My Tickets. Check the salon name at the top.
  2. To change salons, select the salon name or return to My Salons, then select Work Order at the salon you need.
  3. Choose the date. If a ticket is missing, select All to include work that has already started or finished.
  4. Select a ticket from the list, or select View ticket on a new assignment. Check the customer’s name, ticket number, services, prices, service times, and any customer notes.
  5. For an appointment, open My Calendar to review its start time and duration. If the ticket has no appointment or the timing is unclear, confirm it with the front desk.

2. Accept or decline an assigned service

  1. Find your service with the Accept and Decline buttons below it.
  2. Select Accept if you can perform it. Wait for the change to save and check that the Accept and Decline buttons no longer appear for that service. After an error, reopen the ticket to check whether the service was accepted before trying again.
  3. If you cannot take the work, select Decline and confirm. The service returns to the front desk for reassignment. Explain why to the front desk when they need to rearrange the customer’s visit.

How should you read the statuses?

Assigned, In Service, and Completed help you find tickets by the progress of your own work. After your services are complete, the ticket may still include another technician’s work or be waiting for checkout.

If a new assignment is missing

Check the salon, date, and filter first. If a ticket says you are no longer assigned, ask the front desk to check the technician on each service. If the screen shows a loading error, select Try again.

Related: Connect Your Technician Account to a Salon · Start and Complete Services on a Work Order · Track Waiting Customers and Service Progress

title: Start and Complete Services on a Work Order
summary: Update the progress of your services and add completion notes so the front desk knows when to prepare checkout.
htmlContent:
Benefits for technicians and the salon

Recording when you start and finish helps the front desk see which customer you are serving, which services are still in progress, and when to prepare checkout.

Before you start

Open the correct ticket in My Tickets, check the customer’s name, and read the notes. If a service is awaiting your acceptance, select Accept first.

1. Start your services

  1. Review the services assigned to you on the ticket before starting.
  2. When you begin serving the customer, select Start Service at the bottom of the ticket. This starts your services that have not started yet; other technicians’ work stays unchanged.
  3. Check that the status at the top of the ticket changes to In Service.

2. Complete your work and leave notes

  1. When you have finished your services in progress, review your work and select Complete at the bottom of the ticket.
  2. In the completion window, choose a suggested note or enter an Additional note if the salon should remember something about the visit. You may also attach completion photos as described below. Select Confirm Completion after reviewing the notes and finishing any photo uploads.
  3. Check for Completed at the top of the ticket. Only your services in progress are completed; other technicians’ work stays unchanged.
  4. Tell the front desk that your work is finished and share anything they should check before checkout.

Service completion and checkout are separate steps

Completed in your technician account means your work is finished. The front desk or cashier reviews the ticket’s services and takes payment to close the ticket.

For example, you perform a manicure while another technician performs a pedicure for the same customer. Complete your manicure service. The salon checks the pedicure before checking out the customer.

If an action is unavailable

Check whether you have accepted the service, a change is waiting for customer approval, or the ticket is still assigned to you. If Start Service is unavailable, check the ticket date with the front desk. If an action fails, reopen the ticket and check its status before trying again.

Add completion photos, if needed

  1. If you want to show the result of your work, add photos in the completion window. You can also complete the service without photos.
  2. Add up to 5 photos in total, including any already attached.
  3. Wait for all photos to finish uploading. If a photo fails to upload, retry or remove it. You can confirm completion once no photos are uploading or showing an error.
  4. Review the notes and photos, then confirm completion. The front desk can review the saved photos in the ticket, at checkout, or in completed-order details.

Related: View and Accept Your Assigned Tickets · Add, Change, or Remove Work Order Services · Take Payment and Give Customers a Receipt

title: Add, Change, or Remove Work Order Services
summary: Update services at the customer’s request, check prices and service times, and obtain customer approval when prompted.
htmlContent:
Benefits for technicians and customers

Record the customer’s chosen services, prices, and service times so you, the customer, and the cashier can review them before checkout.

Before changing a ticket

Open the correct customer in My Tickets. Discuss the service and price with the customer before making changes. Change only services assigned to you. The salon must enable Technicians can change their own services for you to add, change, or remove services. If it is turned off, ask the front desk to update the ticket. If the customer has not checked in or the ticket has been checked out or canceled, ask the front desk how to handle it.

1. Add, change, or remove a service

  • Add a service: select + Add service, find it in the salon’s catalog, check its price and service time, and confirm your selection.
  • Change a service: select Change on the service and choose its replacement. Check the new service’s price and duration.
  • Add a service outside the catalog: select + Custom, enter its name, price, and service time, then select Add custom service.
  • Remove a service: select Remove, check the name in the confirmation window, and confirm removal. If a service was performed but entered incorrectly, speak with the front desk before removing it.

Changing or removing a service also removes its add-ons from the ticket. Review these items and tell the front desk if they need to be added again.

2. Obtain customer approval when prompted

  1. If a change shows Pending Approval, review the added or replacement service with the customer.
  2. Ask the customer to enter the Last 4 phone digits matching the phone number on the ticket, then select Approve.
  3. Wait for the change to save and check the ticket’s services. If the customer does not agree, select Cancel in the approval section.

This approval step applies to services the salon has marked as requiring confirmation. Services without that requirement and custom services save directly; check the result after saving. Remove uses a removal confirmation window.

Services you add yourself are already accepted for you. When beginning the work, select Start Service at the bottom of the ticket.

3. Tell the front desk about the change

Review the service list, Service total, and service times after updating. Tell the front desk if the price or service time changed so they can check the ticket and arrange upcoming customers.

If a service or approval is unavailable

Check whether the service is included in your work skills at this salon. To update them, open My Salons → Edit Work Skill, or ask the owner to check. If the last 4 phone digits do not match, ask the front desk to check the customer’s details on the ticket. After a save error, check the ticket before adding the service again.

Related: Connect Your Technician Account to a Salon · Start and Complete Services on a Work Order · Coordinate with Your Salon During a Shift

title: View Your Appointments in My Calendar
summary: Choose a salon and day to see your assigned customers, appointment times, service durations, and related tickets.
htmlContent:
Benefits for technicians

See who is booked with you, their start times, and expected service durations so you can prepare for your shift and each customer.

What does this calendar show?

My Calendar shows appointments assigned to you at the selected salon. Use it to review customer appointments. To change your working hours or an appointment time, speak with the person managing the salon’s schedule.

1. Choose a salon and day

  1. Sign in to your technician account and open My Calendar.
  2. If you are linked to several salons, select the correct one from the list.
  3. Select Today for today’s schedule, select a day in the date strip, or use the arrows to view the previous or next day.

2. Review an appointment and open its ticket

  1. Check the customer’s name, service, appointment time, service duration, ticket number, and status.
  2. Select an appointment to open its Work Order. Read the customer notes and check your services before starting.
  3. If appointments overlap or the service time is unsuitable, tell the front desk the customer’s name, ticket number, and displayed time.

When a customer changes their time or the salon changes technicians

Agree on the change with the front desk first. The person managing the salon’s schedule updates the appointment time or assigned technician. Reopen the calendar and ticket to check the updated details.

If your calendar is empty or will not load

Check the salon and date. Tickets without an appointment time may not appear in My Calendar; open My Tickets to check your assigned work. An empty calendar does not mean the salon has no customers to serve.

If the screen says no salon is linked, check My Salons. If it shows a loading error, select Try again.

Related: View and Accept Your Assigned Tickets · Start and Complete Services on a Work Order · Create and Update Appointments

title: Coordinate with Your Salon During a Shift
summary: Chat with your salon, respond to front desk calls, and hand off customer and service details before checkout.
htmlContent:
Benefits for the salon and technicians

Keep everyone informed about who is serving each customer, when a technician can take the next customer, and what needs updating before checkout.

1. Agree on work before the shift

  • Owner or manager: check account connections, the services each technician can perform, and working hours.
  • Front desk: update appointments, assign services to the right technicians, and check their acceptance responses.
  • Technician: check the selected salon, today’s appointments, assigned services, and customer notes. Tell the front desk promptly if you cannot take an assignment.

2. Communicate through chat

  1. As a technician, open My Salons, find the correct linked salon, and select Chat to message the salon.
  2. On the salon side, open the staff list, find the correct technician, and select their chat button.
  3. Be specific: include the customer’s name, ticket number, relevant service, and what you need. For example: “LINH’s ticket needs another 15 minutes. Please check the next customer’s appointment time.”

After agreeing on a change, the person responsible updates the appointment or ticket, and the other person checks the result. Use chat to discuss work and keep the calendar and ticket details accurate.

3. Respond when the front desk calls

When a front desk beep appears, check the salon name and message, then choose the appropriate response:

  • On my way: when you can come to the front desk.
  • Busy — give me a few minutes: when you need more time; select an estimated number of minutes on the screen.
  • Can’t come: when you cannot come; add a reason if needed and select Send.

Wait for the success message to confirm that your response was sent. Dismiss hides the call on your screen without sending an answer to the front desk. After responding, open your ticket to check the assigned work.

4. Hand off before checkout

  1. Check that the services you performed are marked done. Tell the front desk about added services, price changes, or notes to keep.
  2. When several technicians serve the customer, each checks their own services, and the front desk checks the whole ticket.
  3. The front desk or cashier reviews the services and takes payment. Ask the person responsible at the salon to handle appointment changes, technician changes, or tickets already checked out.

When your information does not match the salon’s

Share the ticket number, service date, and the details that differ so you can check them together. If chat is unavailable or a beep is no longer active, contact the front desk directly to confirm the work.
